mbm-1426.clue: I choose the green under the red.
mbm-1426.quote: I embroidered a row of flowers on a pollera sleeve for my cousin. One dark green leaf sticks out farther than the others. My grandmother recognized the bend from the mango tree outside her kitchen.

mbm-1427.clue: I don’t need a clock on our campsite.
mbm-1427.quote: At dawn the sun reaches the silver rim of our cooking pot before it reaches the tent. My brother wakes me when the rim shines. Breakfast has never needed a louder alarm.

mbm-1428.clue: I designed a hole with a living hazard.
mbm-1428.quote: Our mini-golf course runs beside a flowerbed. A very slow tortoise lives there and occasionally crosses the green. We all take a break, even when our favorite scores are on the line.

mbm-1429.clue: I’m the keeper of the first wrong note.
mbm-1429.quote: Our garage band recorded its first rehearsal on a cassette. We began in three different keys and burst out laughing. I always leave those five seconds at the front when I make copies.

mbm-1430.clue: I know when a disc is coming by its shadow.
mbm-1430.quote: We toss a flying disc along a whitewashed wall at dusk. The big oval shadow reaches me a heartbeat before the disc does. My nephew says I have a very tall invisible teammate.

mbm-1431.clue: I fold the napkin for the first arepa.
mbm-1431.quote: When my grandmother taught me, she drew a little pocket in the air with two fingers to show me where the filling goes. I make that same shape with the napkin before I hand the first one to her.

mbm-1432.clue: There are guppies somewhere missing a groundskeeper.
mbm-1432.quote: Our homemade mini-golf hill lost some felt in the wind. We painted the bare wood blue, and the first rain left a real water hazard at the foot of the hill. My cousin lent us his aquarium net. I love hearing him announce another rescue.

mbm-1433.clue: I press my shirt along the tickets.
mbm-1433.quote: In the pocket of my ballroom shirt I keep two ticket stubs from the first social I attended. The paper corners press a little square into the cloth. My partner calls it my private dance medal.

mbm-1434.clue: I hear the old dance floor through my shoes.
mbm-1434.quote: The club has one oak board that hums when the bass is strong. I keep one heel on it when I can. Even if the room is too loud to hear anything else, that board helps me find the beat.

mbm-1435.clue: I fixed the calendar with a paperclip.
mbm-1435.quote: My program drew the days of the month starting in the wrong column. I bent a paperclip into a little pointer to follow the grid on the screen. The first correct month got a paperclip trophy taped to my monitor.

mbm-1436.clue: I put a red pebble on the page.
mbm-1436.quote: I lounge in the sun with a fat paperback and a pebble to stop the pages turning. By evening the pebble is still warm. I fold it in my towel like a little spare piece of the afternoon.

mbm-1437.clue: I draw the footprints after the chase.
mbm-1437.quote: At anime club I like imagining what the street looks like a second after the hero runs off. My sketch shows muddy footprints and one small dog inspecting them. Everybody knew which chase it was.

mbm-1438.clue: I climb for the little blue square.
mbm-1438.quote: There’s a blue square at the top of our gym wall where my friend taped a picture of the sky. On rainy days I can look up from the mat and see exactly where I’d like to be.

mbm-1439.clue: I don’t throw away the broken tee.
mbm-1439.quote: I sharpened the bottom of a snapped wooden tee and used it to mark my score in wet sand. The wind softened the numbers before we left. My partner remembers the round as one long tie.

mbm-1440.clue: I got my lines from the mayor’s dog.
mbm-1440.quote: I played a postman who’s always chased offstage in our comedy. The town mayor lent us his sleepy old terrier. I did all the running while the dog stood in the spotlight accepting applause.

mbm-1441.clue: I write stories as postcards first.
mbm-1441.quote: I give myself one small card to describe a whole town before I start a story there. My current town fits between a drawing of a chimney and a stamp with a pear on it.

mbm-1442.clue: I learned a call sign with a hand drum.
mbm-1442.quote: I kept reversing two letters when writing down a radio friend’s call. I tapped the rhythm on a little frame drum beside my receiver. By the next contact my pencil had learned the beat too.

mbm-1443.clue: I saved the cricket ball from the dog twice.
mbm-1443.quote: Our beach game uses a tennis ball, so the dog thought every drive was an invitation. We gave him a second ball. Now he delivers whichever one we need more urgently and keeps the match surprisingly fair.

mbm-1444.clue: I’ve got a dragon afraid of puddles.
mbm-1444.quote: I painted a clear sleeve with a little blue puddle at the bottom. Slide any monster into it and it appears to be hopping over the water. My fierce red dragon has excellent comic timing.

mbm-1445.clue: I went shopping for exactly one cup.
mbm-1445.quote: The flea-market seller had a teacup with a gold bird hidden inside. I chose it because the bird appears only when the cup is almost empty. I’ve started finishing my tea while it’s still warm.

mbm-1446.clue: I made a knot for every crossing.
mbm-1446.quote: I crocheted my friend a long blue scarf on the ferry to work. At each landing I changed the shade of blue. Spread it on a rail and you can trace a whole month of little voyages.

mbm-1447.clue: I save the snow from my goggles in a drawing.
mbm-1447.quote: After a windy downhill run the frost on my goggles left a fern-shaped pattern. I copied it onto my lift ticket before it melted. The ticket looks as though winter signed my name.

mbm-1448.clue: I made the microphone a little coat.
mbm-1448.quote: My radio shack gets drafty after midnight. I crocheted the microphone a bright wool cover for when it’s turned off. My cat sleeps beside it and appears to be waiting for a very important call.

mbm-1449.clue: I mark the crease with my own shadow.
mbm-1449.quote: During our sunset beach cricket game the tide took the line and the stick we’d used. I stood where it had been and we played one more over with my shadow as the crease.

mbm-1450.clue: My worst move landed three inches off the board.
mbm-1450.quote: I play baduk on the veranda with my aunt. In the evening the bamboo blind lays an extra grid of shadows across our table. After I tried to play on the tablecloth, she hung up a sheet and offered me a rematch.
